My plot is small, only a quarter of a timad, so I must be careful with money. I cannot afford much DAP or urea this year — prices at the cooperative are high — but I will put the manure from our ox and goats on the field before planting, like my mother taught me. I will keep the local sorghum seed I saved from last harvest because it stands the dry spell better than the new kinds, and we have no irrigation here, only the belg and meher rains. My husband and I will do the weeding and bird-scaring ourselves; sorghum needs much watching when the heads fill, so I will sit in the field with the children.
